rated_messages.input_message: Try to stop smoking by setting yourself a rule. For example, "IF I am tempted, THEN I will chew on some mints" - make your own rule that will work for you.
Imagine your 'you' from next year has come to visit, and guess what? You quit! How good is that?
Each time you let an urge pass without smoking, you break the old habit a bit more.

When running a marathon, the hardest part is often towards the end, but many runners stick with it, knowing that the pain will pass. Learning to quit smoking is like running a marathon - if it gets hard, you may be closer to succeeding than you realize!
Think of your anxious mind like a toddler throwing a tantrum. The best way to respond is to quietly watch, but not give in.

Think about what is really important to you. Maybe it's spending time with family or a friend, exercising, doing something spiritual, or creating something. Whatever it is, take a step in that direction.

Pause. Notice the feelings you are having without judgement. Let them come and go. Being aware of your feelings means you can make a new choice about how you respond to your urges instead of smoking on autopilot.

Sometimes an urge comes on like a wave. Imagine what it is like to ride the wave as it ebbs and flows. Instead of trying to swim against it, try riding it out until it disappears into the sea.
If you usually smoke while you talk on the phone, keep a pen and paper nearby to occupy your hands with doodling rather than smoking.
Stop! Breathe. What is going on around you? Inside you? Allow everything to be just as it is. Breathe again.
